title: [spec-gap][R-LOADNG-018/002/003] Python LOADng discovery never driven: originate_rreq has no production caller, no ring progression, no wait/retry loop
description:
Spec B2.1/B2.5: RREQ_WAIT_TIME 5000 ms between attempts, RREQ_RETRIES 3, expanding ring 4->8->15. Classification: not-implemented (python runtime wiring).

Evidence: LoadngRouter.originate_rreq (python/src/lichen/loadng/discovery.py:130-145) has no production caller (only python/tests/loadng/test_discovery.py). Router.route() returns RouteDecision.QUEUE on gradient miss (python/src/lichen/routing/router.py:557-567) but nothing converts QUEUE into originate_rreq + RREQ transmission, and LoadngRouter has no ring-progression or retry state machine at all. node.py contributes only pending_timeout_ms=5000 (node.py:242, queue expiry) and RREQ jitter (node.py:1738-1773, tested python/tests/loadng/test_rreq_jitter.py). C and Rust both implement the ring state machine (lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/loadng.c:550-630; rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs:322-390).

Suggested placement: python/src/lichen/node.py (or routing/router.py): on QUEUE, originate ring RREQ and send via scheduled_send (jitter), advance to next ring after RREQ_WAIT_TIME, fail after EXPANDING_RING exhaustion, then apply Yggdrasil fallback per 05-routing 10.1.
